h: Caves, a Castle and Waterfall Country
p: A visit to the sanctuary works best when you go in with the right mindset. This isn't about watching animals perform or ticking off a list of species; it's about seeing rescued primates living calmly in a place that's dedicated to their welfare. Take time to read the information about each animal's background, as that's where the real heart of the place lies, and encourage children to watch quietly and notice how the chimps interact with each other. It's a gentle, thoughtful day.

Practically speaking, wear boots or wellies, as hill-farm ground can get muddy, and bring layers for the changeable weather of the upper Swansea Valley. A flask and a picnic can be handy, and keep some change for donations or the shop, as every bit helps the sanctuary carry on its work.

The surrounding area is a treat for families. The National Showcaves Centre for Wales at Dan yr Ogof, a short drive up the road, has spectacular cave systems to explore, plus a dinosaur park that younger kids adore. Craig-y-nos Country Park, once the grounds of the castle home of opera star Adelina Patti, is perfect for a riverside stroll. Waterfall fans can head for Henrhyd Falls near Coelbren, a slender drop into a wooded gorge that famously starred as the entrance to the Batcave in The Dark Knight Rises.
Heading back towards Swansea, Mumbles and the Gower Peninsula are ideal for a seaside finish.
It's a properly rewarding corner of Wales to explore.
